{
 "cwd": "/workspace",
 "query": "FULL WEBSITE BRIEF – PAWS & PORCHES PET-FRIENDLY PROPERTY SHOWCASE

Create a classic, polished static website for a fictional pet-focused real-estate listing brand called “Paws & Porches”. The site helps pet owners browse beautiful pet-friendly homes, apartments, cottages, and small estates. This is NOT a real booking platform and does not need backend, accounts, maps API, payment, database, live listings, login, or real estate integrations. Use only static/mock/sample content inside the front-end.

GENERAL STYLE
- Classic real-estate website look, elegant and trustworthy, not futuristic
- Warm neutral palette: cream, soft white, charcoal, muted sage green, light tan, gold accent
- Pet-friendly but still premium: subtle paw details, tasteful icons, cozy home photography placeholders
- Inspiration: clean Instagram-style visual cards and square listing thumbnails, but do not connect to Instagram or use its API
- Simple UI, easy to scan, mobile friendly
- Smooth page transitions between sections/pages, gentle fade/slide animations, not too flashy
- Use static images/placeholders, static listing data, static testimonials

TECH / DELIVERY
- Build as a static React website
- Can be a single page with separate routed-looking sections OR multiple static pages, but must render without server services
- No authentication, no admin, no CRUD, no database
- No external APIs, no live maps, no live search needed
- Mock data is enough for all listings, neighborhoods, agents, reviews, and stats

BRAND
Name: Paws & Porches
Tagline: “Homes chosen with paws in mind.”
Tone: caring, classic, professional, pet-owner friendly
Logo idea: simple house outline with a small paw in the doorway, text beside it

SITE STRUCTURE
1. Header / Navigation
- Left: logo + Paws & Porches
- Nav links: Home, Listings, Pet Features, Neighborhoods, Stories, Contact
- Button: “View Pet-Friendly Homes”
- Sticky header after scroll if possible
- Mobile hamburger menu is fine, but static only

2. Hero Section
Headline: “Find a Home Where Every Paw Feels Welcome”
Subheadline: “A curated collection of pet-friendly homes, apartments, and cozy retreats designed for people who never move without their pets.”
CTA buttons:
- Browse Listings
- See Pet Features
Hero visual:
- Classic real estate photo card layout, maybe one large home image and two smaller pet lifestyle cards
- Add small stat badges: “36 curated homes”, “Dog yards”, “Cat-safe balconies”, “Walkable parks”
- Add subtle page transition / entrance animation

3. Featured Listings Section
Create 6 static listing cards with realistic mock data. Each card should include:
- Property image placeholder
- Listing title
- Location
- Price
- Beds / Baths / Sq ft
- Pet tags like “Fenced Yard”, “Near Dog Park”, “Cat Balcony”, “Mudroom”, “Pet Wash Station”
- Short description
- Button: “View Details” (can open static detail-style section/card or anchor, no backend)

Example listing names:
- Willow Lane Garden Cottage
- Maple & Meadow Townhome
- The Parkside Brick Apartment
- Oak Hollow Family House
- Sunny Courtyard Loft
- Cedar Creek Pet Retreat

4. Listing Detail Preview Section
Make one elegant featured listing detail area for “Willow Lane Garden Cottage”. Include:
- Large photo grid like an Instagram carousel style, but static
- Price: $485,000
- Location: Asheville, North Carolina
- Details: 3 beds, 2 baths, 1,720 sq ft
- Pet highlights: fully fenced garden, dog wash nook, scratch-resistant flooring, sunny cat window ledge, close to walking trails
- Short paragraph description
- Button: “Schedule a Static Preview” or “Download Sample Brochure” but it should not actually submit anywhere

5. Pet Features Section
A section explaining what makes a property pet-friendly:
- Secure fenced outdoor space
- Durable floors
- Nearby parks and walking paths
- Pet washing or mudroom areas
- Quiet corners for nervous pets
- Balcony safety for cats
Use simple classic line icons or emoji-like minimal icons, but keep it refined.

6. Neighborhoods Section
Static cards for pet-friendly neighborhoods:
- Greenfield Row – best for daily walks
- Lakeview Commons – best for active dogs
- Old Market District – best for apartment cats and small pets
- Pine & Stone Village – best for families with multiple pets
Each card includes a small summary, walkability score mock number, nearby pet amenities list.
No maps, only static content.

7. Instagram-Inspired Gallery Section
Title: “Life at Paws & Porches”
Create a grid of 9 square image cards, like an Instagram feed aesthetic.
Content examples:
- dog on porch
- cat by window
- keys next to leash
- garden gate
- cozy living room
- pet bed in mudroom
- morning walk street
- house exterior
- family with pets
This is only visual inspiration, no live Instagram feed, no external connection.
Add captions on hover or below cards.

8. Testimonials / Stories Section
Classic testimonial cards from fictional pet owners:
- “We finally found a home with room for our two rescue dogs.” – Amelia R.
- “The cat-safe balcony checklist was exactly what we needed.” – Jordan & Priya
- “It felt like a real estate site that understood our pets were family.” – Marcus T.
Include small circular avatar placeholders.

9. Simple Search / Filter Visual Area
Add a non-functional but visually useful static filter bar near listings:
- Location dropdown visual
- Pet type dropdown visual: Dog, Cat, Multiple Pets
- Feature dropdown visual: Yard, Balcony, Park Nearby
- Price range visual
- Search button
Important: this is only static front-end UI / mock filter, no real filtering required unless simple client-side filtering from static array is easy. No backend.

10. Contact / CTA Section
Headline: “Ready to Picture Your Pet at Home?”
Text: “Browse our sample collection or send us a note about the kind of pet-friendly space you love.”
Include a simple static contact form layout with fields Name, Email, Pet Type, Message, but no backend submission. It can show a small fake success message on click if purely front-end.
CTA button: “Start Exploring”

11. Footer
- Logo
- Short brand description
- Links: Listings, Pet Features, Neighborhoods, Stories, Contact
- Social labels only: Instagram, Pinterest, Facebook (no real integrations needed)
- Small disclaimer: “Demo static website with sample listings only.”

ANIMATION / INTERACTION
- Smooth page transitions between sections/routes
- Soft fade-in when cards appear
- Hover lift on listing cards
- Smooth scroll navigation
- Gallery hover captions
- Optional static modal/card for listing detail, but no server

CONTENT QUALITY
- Use realistic real-estate copy
- Keep the design simple but complete
- Avoid overly modern neon or tech startup look
- Must feel like a finished marketing/listing website someone could show to a real estate client
- All data should be hardcoded sample content

FINAL EXPECTATION
Deliver a clean static React website for Paws & Porches with classic styling, pet-focused real-estate listing cards, Instagram-inspired gallery visuals, and smooth page transitions. No backend, no APIs, no login, no database, no real-time features.",

 },

  "Paws & Porches",
  "Homes chosen with paws in mind.",
  "View Pet-Friendly Homes",
  "Find a Home Where Every Paw Feels Welcome",
  "36 curated homes",
  "Dog yards",
  "Cat-safe balconies",
  "Walkable parks"
 ]
}

"""Grade a Webdev task as the explorer does (verl recipes/design webdev-eval): render, shrink, judge.

No index.html in dist/ scores 0. A render that fails, or a judge that never answers, writes no reward (not scored):
neither says anything about the page."""
import base64
import io
import json
import os
import random
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, "/tests")
os.environ["WEBDEV_GRADE_HTTP"] = "1"   # serve over loopback http so React/Vue/ES-module sites actually run
from webdev.eval_rubric import build_prompt  # noqa: E402
from webdev.shot import _build_shot_cmd, _parse_render_env, _parse_shot_b64  # noqa: E402
from webdev.verdict import parse_verdict  # noqa: E402

cfg = json.loads(Path("/tests/grade.json").read_text())
V = Path("/logs/verifier")
V.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
dist = Path(cfg["cwd"]) / "dist"


def done(reward: float | None, why: str, **extra) -> None:
    (V / "result.json").write_text(json.dumps({"reward": reward, "summary": why, **extra}, indent=1))
    print(why)
    if reward is None:
        print("not scored", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
    (V / "reward.txt").write_text(f"{reward}\n")
    sys.exit(0)


files = sorted(str(p.relative_to(dist)) for p in dist.rglob("*") if p.is_file())[:200] if dist.is_dir() else []
if "index.html" not in files:
    done(0.0, "The agent delivered nothing to dist/." if not files else "dist/ has no index.html, so there is no page to open.",
         delivered=files)
res = subprocess.run(["sh", "-c", _build_shot_cmd(f"file://{dist}/index.html")], capture_output=True, text=True,
                     timeout=150)   # SHOT_TIMEOUT_S
shot = {"output": (res.stdout or "") + "\n" + (res.stderr or "")}
shot_b64, console_errors = _parse_shot_b64(shot)
render_env = _parse_render_env(shot)
if render_env.get("proxy_failed") or not shot_b64:
    print(shot["output"][-2000:], file=sys.stderr)
    done(None, "external assets were unreachable on every route" if render_env.get("proxy_failed")
         else "the screenshot produced no image")
jpg = base64.b64decode(shot_b64)
try:   # eval_mode._shrink: the judge refuses shots over 20 MP; proportional, quality 75
    from PIL import Image
    Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS = None
    im = Image.open(io.BytesIO(jpg))
    size = im.size
    if im.width * im.height > 20e6:
        k = (20e6 / (im.width * im.height)) ** 0.5
        im = im.convert("RGB").resize((max(1, int(im.width * k)), max(1, int(im.height * k))), Image.LANCZOS)
        b = io.BytesIO(); im.save(b, "JPEG", quality=75); jpg = b.getvalue(); size = im.size
except ImportError:
    size = None
(V / "screenshot.jpg").write_bytes(jpg)
# webdev-structural-gate@1: necessary conditions, not a replacement judge.
_gate_layout = {}
for _line in (shot["output"] or "").splitlines():
    if _line.startswith("LAYOUT:"):
        try:
            _gate_layout = json.loads(_line[len("LAYOUT:"):])
        except (ValueError, TypeError):
            pass
        break
if (not isinstance(_gate_layout, dict) or _gate_layout.get("error")
        or not isinstance(_gate_layout.get("text"), str)
        or not isinstance(_gate_layout.get("scroll_w"), (int, float))
        or not isinstance(_gate_layout.get("client_w"), (int, float))
        or _gate_layout["client_w"] <= 0):
    done(None, "Structural measurements unavailable; not scored.")
_gate_text = " ".join(_gate_layout["text"].split())
_gate_kw = cfg.get("gate_keywords") or []
_gate_fails = []
if not _gate_text:
    _gate_fails.append("blank rendered DOM")
if _gate_kw and not any(_kw.casefold() in _gate_text.casefold() for _kw in _gate_kw):
    _gate_fails.append("no brief-keyword DOM presence")
if _gate_layout["scroll_w"] > _gate_layout["client_w"] + 1:
    _gate_fails.append("horizontal overflow")
_gate_report = {"passed": not _gate_fails, "failed": _gate_fails,
                "dom_chars": len(_gate_text), "keywords": _gate_kw,
                "layout": _gate_layout}
(V / "structural_gates.json").write_text(json.dumps(_gate_report, indent=1))
if _gate_fails:
    done(0.0, "Structural gates failed: " + "; ".join(_gate_fails),
         structural_gates=_gate_fails)
content = [{"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:image/jpeg;base64," + base64.b64encode(jpg).decode()}},
           {"type": "text", "text": build_prompt().format(query=cfg["query"][:1500])}]   # QUERY_CAP
url = os.environ.get("WEBDEV_JUDGE_URL", "https://router.huggingface.co/v1").rstrip("/") + "/chat/completions"
_judge_pin = cfg["judge"]
if os.environ.get("WEBDEV_JUDGE_REVISION") != _judge_pin["model_sha"]:
    done(None, "Judge deployment revision is unbound; not scored.")
(V / "judge_config.json").write_text(json.dumps(_judge_pin, indent=1))
body = json.dumps({"model": cfg["judge"]["request_model"], "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 1024,  # webdev-temp0-pin@1
                   "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": content}]}).encode()
verdict, last = None, ""
for attempt in range(4):   # JUDGE_RETRIES, with eval_mode's backoff
    if attempt:
        time.sleep(min(60.0, 3.0 * (3 ** (attempt - 1))) * (0.5 + random.random()))
    try:
        req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=body, method="POST", headers={
            "Content-Type": "application/json", "Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ.get('WEBDEV_JUDGE_KEY', '')}"})
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=180) as r:   # JUDGE_TIMEOUT_S
            _judge_reply = json.loads(r.read())
            if _judge_reply.get("model_revision") != _judge_pin["model_sha"]:
                done(None, "Judge response revision differs from the task pin; not scored.")
            msg = _judge_reply["choices"][0]["message"]
        v = parse_verdict(msg.get("content") or msg.get("reasoning_content") or "")
        if "_failed" not in v:
            verdict = v
            break
        last = v["_failed"]
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
        last = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"[:200]
if not verdict:
    done(None, f"judge unavailable: {last}")
done(verdict["score"], verdict.get("reason", ""), dims=verdict["dims"], visual=verdict["visual"], screenshot_size=size,
     console_errors=console_errors[:1500] if console_errors not in ("", "[]") else "")

rationale: Gate trivial, off-brief and overflowing pages to a scored 0 before the vision call, cutting judge spend and the blank-page lottery. Passing pages reach the judge unchanged.

gate_keywords: Homes chosen with paws in mind.
